replying_to: Replying to Enhancing Transformer Efficiency for Multivariate Time Series Classification
display_title: Official Review of Paper3186 by Reviewer GKXP

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors propose a mixing framework based on Transformer and Fourier transform. By pruning each module of the network separately and sequentially, the paper investigates the impact of each module on predictive accuracy. The paper conducts comprehensive experiments on 18 benchmark MTS datasets. Ablation studies are used to evaluate the impact of each module. Through module-by-module pruning, the results demonstrate the trade-offs between efficiency and effectiveness, as well as the efficiency and complexity of the network. Finally, we evaluate, via Pareto analysis, the trade-off between network efficiency and performance.
content.main_review:
Strengths: 
1. Develop the first mixing model architecture based on attention and Fourier transform for processing MTS data.
2. Experimental results indicate the trade-off between model efficiency and its effectiveness, as well as its complexity.
3. Propose to investigate the trade-off between efficiency and performance using Pareto analysis. 

Weaknesses:
1. The motivation is unclear. The authors claim that the proposed method can work on high-dimensional or long-sequential time series. However, the datasets used in the paper do not support such a strong assumption. 
2. Baselines are weak, some representative methods mentioned in related work are not included in the experimental comparison. 
2. More theoretical studies are expected. It would be better to analyze the proposed method quantitatively and explain why and how to tune the parameters between DFT and Transformer.
content.summary_of_the_review: This work proposes a mixing network based on Transformer and Fourier transform for MTS classification. Experiments are conducted on 18 MTS datasets, including ablation studies on different modules of the network, module-by-module pruning evaluated in terms of the predictive performance, training speed, and the number of learnable parameters.  However, the paper lacks theoretical studies, why combining DFT and Transform is efficient is not discussed. Plus, more datasets can be used as the testbed of high-dimensional or long-sequential time series, as claimed the main strength of the proposed model.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.

content.summary_of_the_paper: Paper solves the time-series classification problem in a computationally efficient way using modified transformer architecture that includes the Fourier transform inside the transformer block.
content.main_review:
The topic of the paper is interesting, the architectural approach makes sense. I have two major concerns about the paper.
- The architectural approach is not novel. In this paper (note it already has 30 citations): https://arxiv.org/pdf/2105.03824.pdf the FFT has already been used to accelerate Transformer. Moreover, I find the approach of the arxiv paper more elegant and potentially more compute efficient, since they entirely remove the self-attention layer and unlike the current approach they do FFT only once per block. I don't understand, by the way, why FFT is done twice in the current approach?
- The empirical results only include the ablation study of the proposed approach. I do not see any accuracy and compute efficiency comparisons with existing approaches. The empirical results are not at all convincing.
content.summary_of_the_review: I recommend reject, because novelty is limited and empirical results are unconvincing.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.

replying_to: Replying to Enhancing Transformer Efficiency for Multivariate Time Series Classification
display_title: Official Review of Paper3186 by Reviewer Wddd

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The paper proposed a transformer-based architecture for time series classification.
The architecture consists of 1D convolutional embedding followed by multiple encoders, each encoder consists of 2D Fast Fourier transform followed by Inverse Fast Fourier transform then the typical multi-head attention and a feed-forward layer after the encoders there is a global averaging pooling layer to the output over the entire time dimension and a linear layer used for classification. The paper investigates the effect of each layer on the efficiency and its effectiveness by layer by layer pruning and calculating the accuracy after pruning each layer long with the number of parameters and training time. The paper investigates the trade-off between efficiency and performance using Pareto analysis. Experiments were done on 18 datasets.
content.main_review:
Strength:  
1- The paper applied the proposed architecture to 18 datasets.  
2- The ablation study investigating the effect each layer has on accuracy and efficiency was interesting and informative.  
3- The use of Pareto analysis to analyze the accuracy and efficiency was novel.  

Weakness:

1- Missing a lot of related work including informer[1], log sparse transformer[2], Reformer[3] all of which are transformer-based architecture designed to enhance the efficiency of the typical transformer.  
2- It is unclear what the is purpose of FFT directly followed by IFFT don't they cancel the effect of each other?  
3- It is unclear why the proposed architecture does not contain a typical add and normalize layer (is it for efficiency reasons).  
4- There was no comparison with other baseline transformers in terms of accuracy and efficiency.  
5- The novelty of the work is very limited, the difference between a typical transformer is the FFT directly followed by IFFT and the removal add and normalize layer (and again there was no discussion on why this is particularly useful).  
 

[1]Zhou, Haoyi, et al. "Informer: Beyond efficient transformer for long sequence time-series forecasting." Proceedings of AAAI. 2021.  
[2]Li, Shiyang, et al. "Enhancing the locality and breaking the memory bottleneck of transformer on time series forecasting." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 32 (2019): 5243-5253.  
[3] Kitaev, Nikita, Łukasz Kaiser, and Anselm Levskaya. "Reformer: The efficient transformer." arXiv preprint arXiv:2001.04451 (2020).
content.summary_of_the_review:
My main concerns are the following:
The paper proposed an interesting way to measure the efficiency and accuracy of each layer in the proposed transformer. 
But it is unclear why the proposed architecture is more efficient than a typical transformer. There was also no comparison with other baselines transformers in terms of accuracy or efficiency. So basically, the paper is an analysis of different layers of a transformer. This makes the significance and the novelty of the paper quite low.

replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Paper3186 by Reviewer Wddd

content.title: Thank you for your review
content.comment:
Thank you for your comments! Please find our responses below:

$\textbf{W1: Missing a lot of related work.}$

Thank you for pointing this out. We will add "efficient" Transformer networks in Section 2 in the revised manuscript.

$\textbf{W2: It is unclear what is the purpose of FFT directly followed by IFFT don't they cancel the effect of each other.}$

Thank you for pointing out the mistake in the paper writing. We will correct it in the revised manuscript. Between 2D FFT and 2D IFFT, we have the self-attention layer. After FFT converts the features to the frequency domain, the IFFT can map the features to the temporal domain without canceling the effect of each other.

$\textbf{W3: It is unclear why the proposed architecture does not contain a typical add and normalize layer.}$

We do not draw this layer in Figure 1 but include it in Section 3 (see Batch Normalization).

$\textbf{W4: There was no comparison with other baseline transformers in terms of accuracy and efficiency.}$

Our main focus is to propose a method for analyzing the efficiency of a model rather than proposing an "efficient" model. Such an interesting analysis method, which is also acknowledged by the reviewer, is applied to the MTSC problem in this paper. Hence, we do not compare our "model" with existing approaches due to our focus on how to analyze the efficiency-performance trade-off of a model rather than comparing it with "efficient" Transformers which focus on modifying the original Transformer architecture mentioned by the reviewer.

$\textbf{W5: The novelty of the work is very limited.}$
The "model" itself in Section 3 is not the most critical part of this paper. Our work makes use of the Transformer architecture and FFT and then decomposes it into 8 modules. We mainly focus on analyzing the "contribution" of each module in the multivariate time series classification task and use Pareto analysis to analyze the accuracy-efficiency trade-off. This work can be generalized to study any recent approaches applied in different domains.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper studies multivariate time series classification by combining signal processing (Fast Fourier Transform and Inverse Fourier Transform) and machine learning (CNN) approaches. Authors make analysis of the impact of each component to the efficiency and accuracy of classification by conducting ablation study, pruning and pareto analysis.
content.main_review:
Strenghts:

1. The main idea of making analysis of the efficiency and accuracy is interesting
2. For reproducibility of the approach, the implementation details are provided

Weaknesses:

1. The decrease in accuracy is quite high with component pruning
2. The analysis discussion is poor especially in Section 4.7 Pareto Analysis, which is listed as contribution of this paper
3. After the analysis there is no clear proposed model for an efficient model 
4. There is no comparison to efficient other approaches
5. The choice of time series datasets, almost half of the time series have length of less than 100-150 data points. It is not clear if the analysis applies to much longer time series dataset

The paper misses the comparison to the efficient time series models with sparse attention.
Li, S., Jin, X., Xuan, Y., Zhou, X., Chen, W., Wang, Y. X., & Yan, X. (2019). Enhancing the locality and breaking the memory bottleneck of transformer on time series forecasting. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 32, 5243-5253.
Wu, S., Xiao, X., Ding, Q., Zhao, P., Ying, W. E. I., & Huang, J. (2020). Adversarial Sparse Transformer for Time Series Forecasting.

The lengths of the datasets chosen for Pareto analysis are 50 (Finger Movements) and 405 (Heartbeat). As the efficiency becomes more important for longer time series, it would be interesting to see the Pareto analysis for longer time series, see Table 3 in Appendix.
content.summary_of_the_review: Although the efficiency analysis idea is interesting, the discussion of the results is poor (see Section 4.7), it is not clear what authors suggest to use as a final optimal model. Furthermore, one expects to see “the proposed model” to be compared to the existing approaches in terms of accuracy and efficiency. There is no comparison to the existing approaches, only the analysis of the impact of each component to the accuracy and efficiency of the model. Currently, it is not clear if the proposed approach is better than the existing approaches. I believe the paper can be submitted to other venues after improving the conclusions of the analysis and completing the experiments with comparison to existing approaches.

content.title: Thank you for your review
content.comment:
Thank you for your comments! Please find our responses below:

$\textbf{W1: The decrease in accuracy is quite high with component pruning.}$

As mentioned in the paper, some components (MHA, FFT, IFFT) demonstrate a notable influence on the model performance on average. This helps us identify important modules of a model. For more complex models, the issue of model redundancy can be more serious, and thus identifying key modules for such models is important. It should be expected that some modules have larger contributions to the model performance than other modules.

$\textbf{W2: The analysis discussion is poor especially in Section 4.7 Pareto Analysis.}$

There is no such final optimal model even through Pareto analysis. It serves as a tool to analyze the trade-off between performance and efficiency. Specifically, such analysis helps us recognize that how many computational resources are required in order for a model to achieve a certain performance. Conversely, we know that how well can a model perform given a certain amount of resources.

$\textbf{W3: After the analysis there is no clear proposed model for an efficient model.}$

Our main focus is to propose a method for analyzing the efficiency of a model rather than proposing an efficient model. 

$\textbf{W4: There is no comparison to efficient other approaches.}$

In this work, we propose an interesting method, which is also acknowledged by the reviewer, for which we use this method to evaluate the trade-off between efficiency and accuracy for the multivariate time series classification (MTSC) problem. The "model" itself in Section 3 is not the most critical part of this paper. Such a trade-off analysis method (module-by-module pruning and Pareto analysis) is applied to the MTSC problem in this paper. It can also be generalized to study any recent approaches applied in different domains. Hence, we do not compare our "model" with existing approaches due to our focus on how to analyze the efficiency-performance trade-off of a model.

$\textbf{W5: It is not clear if the analysis applies to much longer time series dataset.}$

The availability of UCR/UEA time series (TS) benchmark datasets limits our capacity for choosing longer and larger datasets. Among the datasets (FaceDetection, InsectWings, PenDigits) in which we do not choose in our original paper with data samples greater than 5000, we perform experiments on these datasets, and the same model analysis techniques apply to these data, and we draw similar conclusions as the original paper after adding these larger/longer datasets. We will add the results of these datasets in the revised manuscript.
